retired_at.description: When it was retired; null while active.

updated_by.description: Who made the last write (the create, else the last edit).

version.description: Send it back as the PATCH precondition.

CharacterCreated.description: `201` answer of `POST /api/admin/members/{id}/characters`: the row plus `link`. With module `character_data` on and a Nexon key, a MapleSEA (`msea`) character is linked at once for its member in the same request (active with no member confirmation, a History row as `POST …/link`, then its first Open API fetch, which copies NEXON's class and level into the row by `system:nexon`; the answered row is the one stored after it): `linked`; `failed` when the link could not be written (the character is saved; Link… tries again); `null` when none was made (module off, no key, or another region).

CharacterChoice.description: One of a party member's active characters, a candidate for the run.

CharacterBasis.description: Where the character a member brings comes from, first match wins: `run_pick` the run's own pick (runs only), `timing_pick` the weekly timing's pick (on a run: read live from the run's timing), `main` their roster main, `only` their only active character with no main.

CharacterClash.description: The character brought here also brought on another run of this boss week (the configured reset) for a boss this run has too, at any difficulty: the weekly clear limit. A warning only; a pick always saves. Cancelled runs never clash.

day.description: Day index within the boss week (0 = reset day).

time.description: HH:MM; null for an own-time run.

bosses.description: The other run's boss tokens this run shares by boss.

basis.description: Why the character is on the other run.

RunCharacterSlot.description: One party member on a run or a weekly timing. `candidates` are their active characters (no level filter), oldest first; empty when they have none; `retired` counts the rest (never offered). `picked` is this slot's own stored pick (the run's on a run, the timing's on a timing) while it names a candidate, with `picked_at`/`picked_by`. `brings` is the character the member brings, resolved on every read and never stored: on a run its pick, else its timing's pick, else the main, else the only active character; on a timing its pick, else the main, else the only one; null with none. `basis` says which. `version` is the slot version a pick sends back (0 while nothing is stored). `warnings` is always empty on a timing.

TimingCharacters.description: A weekly timing's party slots (modules `roster` and `character_data`).

CharacterPick.description: Request body of `PUT /api/admin/runs/{id}/characters/{member}` and `PUT /api/admin/fixed/{id}/characters/{member}`. `character_id` names one of the member's active characters, or is null to clear the pick (required either way, else 422 `invalid`); `version` is the slot version read (else 422 `version_required`; another is 409 `stale`).

CharacterCreate.description: Request body of `POST /api/admin/members/{id}/characters`. `ign` is 4-12 letters or digits, unique per `world` case-insensitively (retired characters included; else 422 `ign_taken`); `world` is the region, default `msea`; `class` is at most 32 characters (empty: none); `level` 1-300. `class` and `level` are optional manual values: the admin app sends neither for a MapleSEA character while module `character_data` has a Nexon key (the create links it, and each stored NEXON fetch copies NEXON's class and level into the row, where they stay after an unlink or expiry). A member's first active character is their main whatever `role` says; otherwise `role` defaults to `alt`, and `main` takes the crown (the current main becomes an alt in the same write).

CharacterPatch.description: Request body of `PATCH /api/admin/characters/{id}`. `version` is the row version the edit was made from (else 422 `version_required`; another version is 409 `stale`). An omitted field is kept; `class`/`level` `null` (or an empty class) clears it; `retired: true` retires (keeping the first time), `false` restores. `role: main` takes the crown; without `role`, an active character with no other active main becomes the main and a restored main becomes an alt while another main is active. The main cannot be retired or made an alt while the member has other active characters (409 `main_required`).
